name: Well drilling and well pump service

pf.license.need: Pump and well work in a home needs a license where the state or county licenses well drillers and pump installers. New well drilling can need its own driller license. Water line and electrical work can need a plumbing or electrical license too.
pf.license.who holds it: Both: the company (a well and pump contractor license, where the state asks) and each technician (apprentice or journeyman, where the state has levels).
what to ask: The company's license number and class
Each technician's own number and level, in their invite reply
A driller license, for new wells, where the state has one
Any job-size limit the license has
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: The well and pump listing goes live once it's set up. Each technician is offered only once the owner says yes. A job over the license's size limit is never offered or quoted: the owner is told why.
pf.license.renewals: Reminders before each expiry, on the dates the owner picks (the example: 5 weeks and 1 week before). A lapsed license pauses new bookings for that person.
pf.license.insurance or bond: Liability insurance, and a bond where the state's form asks for one: from the state form.
pf.license.background checks: Only where the state's form asks.
pf.license.at the counter: Work done at the counter: the state's form says if it needs a license. Safe default: the company's license on file, shown on the listing.
pf.license.local rules: Some counties require a permit to drill, replace or seal a well, or to change a pump: the form for that place applies, by the customer's address. Water test results go through a certified lab where the rules require it.

pf.services.capacity: One technician per booking. Bigger jobs, like a pump pulled from a deep well, can need a crew of two; the counter's rebuilds need its one test bench.
pf.services.skills each needs: New well drilling needs the driller license and the rig. Pump replacement needs the pump installer license and the pulling rig. Wiring needs an electrician or a license that covers it. Counter rebuilds need the rebuild skill.
pf.services.nobody home: A pump house or well cap outside with its own access: nobody needs to be home. DONE comes with a photo.
pf.services.online: A video check only, where the owner offers it. No repair is done by video.
pf.services.extras: Travel inside the service area only (the example: 40 miles). Parts at cost or at list, the owner's pick. No tax line unless the owner sets a rate.
pf.services.smallest_job: A switch the owner sets: the smallest job taken, with smaller requests pointed elsewhere (the example takes any list job and any quote over $500).

stops the booking.words: A gas smell, hissing, or a carbon monoxide alarm
stops the booking.says: Leave the house now. Then call 911 and the gas company.
stops the booking.booking: No booking. A new request must say the gas company cleared the house.

stops the booking.words: Someone hurt, sparks, a shock from a tap or pipe, or water on the pump's wiring or the control box
stops the booking.says: Get away from the water. Don't touch the pump or its wiring. Call 911.
stops the booking.booking: No booking until it's safe; the customer can come back.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: A pump that runs with no water, or no water at all
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Shut off the pump at the breaker. Running dry harms the pump. Use stored water.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: Water that looks brown, smells like sewage, or came after a flood
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Don't drink or cook with it. Use bottled water until the well is tested.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: A pressure tank bulging, hissing or leaking hard
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Shut off the pump at the breaker and keep away from the tank.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: A flooded well pit or pump house
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Keep the power off at the breaker, and stay out. Don't turn the pump on until it's checked.

pf.visit.proof it's done: The technician texts DONE with the bill's lines, and photos after. After a pump is pulled, the well is disinfected and the water is tested where the rules require it; the result is on the secure page.
pf.visit.permits: Where a permit was pulled, the inspector's visit is set up after the work, and the result is kept with the job.

pf.staff.levels: Apprentice and journeyman, where the state has levels; each person's own license per state, where the state licenses well drillers and pump installers.
pf.staff.supervision: An apprentice works only with a journeyman on the job, where the state's rules require it. An apprentice is never sent alone by default.
pf.staff.special work: New well drilling only by people with the driller license. Pulling a deep pump only with a crew of two. Wiring only by people whose license covers it.
pf.staff.who OKs what: The owner OKs fees, quotes over the limit, new well jobs and same-day jobs. After hours, a job sent now goes to the technician on call, then the backup set at sign-up. An office manager may OK prices if the owner sets it.
pf.staff.stand-ins: Another technician with the same skill and level, at the same window and price.

pf.rules.written estimate: A written estimate before work above an amount: from the state form.
pf.rules.right to cancel: A written right to cancel for work sold at the home: where the rules require it.
pf.rules.permits: Pulled by the business where the local rules require one; the inspection follows.
pf.rules.well rules: Where the rules require it: the well is disinfected after the pump is pulled, an old well is sealed by a licensed driller, and the driller's report goes to the county.
pf.rules.license on papers: The license number on quotes and bills: from the state form.
pf.rules.digging: A utility locate before any digging: always.
pf.rules.declared emergency: Price limits in a declared emergency: where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.warranty: The owner's own (the example: 1 year on labor), shown on the receipt; the maker's warranty on pumps and tanks.
pf.rules.state notices: A state's own notices for home repairs: from the state form, sent before the work or with the quote.
pf.rules.records: 7 years, as for every kind of work.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for well pumps:
well pumps: The pump runs dry or the water worsens before the visit: the safety steps again, then urgent
A gas smell, or a shock from a tap or pipe, at any point: stop, get out, call 911 and the gas company
After hours: sent now to the technician on call, then the backup; nobody takes it means no visit tonight and nothing charged
Nobody home at the door: the no-show steps, with the owner's OK before any fee
A renter whose landlord pays: the landlord's OK first, or the renter pays instead; a shared well needs every owner's OK
A bigger job found (a failing well casing, a dry well): its own quote, OK'd by the owner over the limit
A water test is positive or odd: not an emergency; no drinking, the result is on the secure page, and the next step is a disinfection and a retest, by quote
A flood or a storm brings many calls: PAUSE, and a declared emergency's price limits
At the counter: a part that can't be rebuilt, a gas part, a pressure tank, or a drop-off nobody picks up

notes:
Started from plumber (pattern: fix, refitted Tue Oct 27 on the frozen master). Flow B is the plumber's usual side: Stonecreek Well, technicians Colm and Felix, at the home. Flow A is the less usual side: Stonecreek Pump, Sam's pump parts and repair counter (the master's Lee's Barbershop), counter techs Lucia and Joel, with a jet pump left as a drop-off. The second kind of work in sign-up (the master's electrical) is water treatment (Stonecreek Water Treatment). Facts: firststeps (a service call, a part check), documents (a written estimate over the owner's amount), sentnow (an after-hours no-water call), dropoff (a pump left at the counter), extrawork, photos, results (a lab result for a water test comes later), video; planbill and forms are not listed (a home warranty plan rarely covers a well; no form is signed first). Switch cancelright in flow B only (work sold at the home). Settings: A a set start, B a 2-hour window.
Flow B main path list|card|bill: a $179 pressure switch replacement (the $89 service call included), a card saved for the $89 fee, only for a late cancel or nobody home, and only if Sam confirms; Rosie texts the bill. The other paths: list|none|bill, list|card|card (the card charged $179 when Colm texts DONE), visit|card|bill (a well pump repair priced at the visit: only the $89 call is promised; the example quote is a pressure switch and gauge $165 plus wire repair $80 = $245), photos|deposit|bill (a pressure tank replacement from photos, $640: $160 deposit, $480 rest, Sam OKs it), list|full|none (a $150 well water test paid in full; the result goes on the secure page, never in a text).
A well pump replacement over the owner's amount is the master's 'an estimate becomes its own job' (B8-62, B8-63): a written estimate and contract, a $2,400 example in two payments (a $600 deposit, 25%, and the $1,800 rest on the final bill after the pump is in and tested), no stage bills (a one-day job; the quote split and the day pick say so with pairs). New well drilling is quoted after a site visit on the same path, with a state permit, a utility locate and the driller license first; the owner OKs each one.
Flow A paths: list|card|counter (main; a $35 pressure switch test, a card saved for the $20 fee), list|none|counter, list|deposit|counter (a $140 jet pump rebuild, $40 deposit and $100 at the counter), list|full|none (a $55 water sample test, paid in full), photos|card|counter (a control box repair from photos, $90, Sam OKs it), visit|card|counter (a pump repair priced at the counter, only the $25 check promised).
After hours: no water at all is sent now to the technician on call, $149 taken off the repair, flat-price jobs $60 more, free cancel until the technician texts OMW (B4-91 words). This is the only sent-now work, so S2-30 keeps its sent-now branch: S2-30's line says well pump service takes jobs sent now and the counter takes none, and S1-21's row names the on-call technician. I searched the joined text for the opposite claim.
Safety: a gas smell, hissing, a carbon monoxide alarm, someone hurt, sparks, a shock from a tap or pipe, or water on the pump's wiring or control box stops the booking (911 first). A pump running dry or no water, brown or bad-smelling water, a bulging or hissing pressure tank, and a flooded pump pit are safety steps and then the booking goes on, marked urgent. The Spanish call (B3-11, B3-18) is about brown, bad-smelling water: the same go-on branch; its advice is to stop drinking it and shut off the pump at the breaker. The hazard card (B8-30) is a cracked well casing, which stops the pump work and sends a written note: it is not a stop word.
Private: a water test result is on the secure page only, never in a text (pf.messages, pf.questions, pf.edges); a positive test is not an emergency: no drinking, a disinfection and a retest by quote. A shared well needs every owner's OK. Nothing names a state, city or law; the well driller, pump installer and electrician licenses, the county permit, the deposit cap, the right to cancel and emergency prices are switches from the state's or county's form. License numbers use an obviously fake format (WP-1042, WT-2210, PS-3305; people WP-10552, WT-10417).
Rename: built from the contractor family's pair map with a fix-style template (the master's plumbing example words become pump words; service call stays 'service call', credited to the repair; the repipe example becomes the pump replacement). 'cut', 'hair' and price-board words are turned into this work's words. The A3-22 / A3-23 lines that said the plug-in has no danger words now name this work's. Second company names stay at 15 characters or less so S1-78 and B10-01 stay under their limits.
keep: pump rebuild (the counter's jet pump rebuild), leak (a roof leak, the work it doesn't do), valve, pipe (a shock from a tap or pipe), electrician (the safety advice), service call (the fix-style visit fee), color (the protected-classes line in S13-40).
Plug-in splits kept whole (splitsKept): the plumber's list, since this work uses every branch: licensed state by state (S1-60, S1-63, S2-28), a pump drop-off names no technician (A7-59, S11-87, S11-90), control box repairs are Lucia's alone (A7-61), a switch test needs the switch (A8-02), the counter or a drop-off (A8-53); in B, an after-hours call is sent now (B4-81, B7-55, B8-58), a written estimate over the amount (B4-57, B5-34), a pump or tank delivered and set up (B8-71), a pump to the counter (B8-72), an outside check partway (B8-65), a permit inspection (B10-29).
